prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1114; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's policyholder after a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the repair shop show damage consistent with the described impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so photos are the main visual record for now.

Entry 4: Police report places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of collision, and the responding officer's notes match the account given to us. Vehicle damage aligns with the reported point and force of impact.

Entry 5: Counsel submitted the initial injury summary, reporting neck strain. The reported injury fits the kind and force of a rear-end impact of this type.

Entry 6: Claimant's account was given in a recorded call and again in the follow-up interview, and the core details were the same both times. Requested the medical records and itemized bills from the treating provider.

Entry 7: Medical records show no prior treatment to the neck or upper back, and our index search returned no earlier claims for the same body area.

Entry 8: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for a neck strain of this severity. Requested the treating physician's notes explaining the expected recovery timeline and the reasons for continued visits.

Entry 9: Reviewed the vehicle's prior repair history and found no earlier damage on record. The repair estimate is being checked against the photos and the reported impact.

Entry 10: Sent a status letter to counsel listing outstanding items: the physician's treatment notes, the final itemized bills, and the repair invoice. Will reassess once these are received.
